key_insight: A passing hardware verification test suite does not guarantee compliance with the specification. Verify the Verifier uses an LLM to cross-check passing simulation traces against the specification, looking for bugs that existing scoreboards miss.
problem_solved: UVM scoreboards check whether hardware behavior agrees with a reference model, but gaps in those checks can let specification-violating bugs pass every test. These hidden failures are called scoreboard escapes.
method: Examine simulation traces from passing UVM regressions using an LLM-based Anomaly Cross-Checker.
Ground the cross-check in the specification rather than relying solely on scoreboard agreement.
Study 564 injected bugs across four OpenTitan IP blocks; the provided abstract identifies 68 as candidates but is truncated before reporting complete results.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners building verification tools, this illustrates how specification-grounded LLMs can complement conventional automated checks. It also highlights why a passing test suite should not be treated as proof of correctness.
visual_elements: Split-path diagram: passing regression → scoreboard agreement versus specification compliance.
Workflow: specification + passing simulation traces → LLM Anomaly Cross-Checker → suspected violations.
Bug slipping through a scoreboard gate, then flagged by a specification-checking magnifying glass.
Evaluation snapshot: four OpenTitan IP blocks and 564 injected bugs, with final detection outcomes marked as unavailable in the excerpt.
paper_title: Verify the Verifier: Specification-Grounded LLM Cross-Checking for Bugs That Escape UVM Scoreboards
paper_authors: Ana E. Sanchez Villalobos, Michael D. Quinn, Aakash Tyagi, Minh D. Luu, David Kebo Houngninou
